contexts.text: Those who placed worship solely in externals were represented by the gentiles, whom they called foreigners, and who were their servants, and performed menial services in the Church; as in, strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the foreigner shall be your ploughmen and your vine-dressers ()... Those who place worship solely in externals are called the sons of the foreigner. Further illustrated.

Sojourner = that he was not born in the land, thus that he is not acknowledged for a native, but is regarded as a stranger... As sojourner is applied to what is regarded as alien, and that is alien which is not in the land or of the land, it follows that it denotes what is rare.
I will bring strangers upon thee (), that is, falsities. ( = falsities which destroy truths. AE 537:16.)
Are we not counted of him strangers, because he hath sold us? () = that he has alienated them, so that they are no longer his.
And he made himself strange to them () = no conjunction because without a medium.
Where it is said that the Lord makes himself strange to the people... it is meant that they make themselves strangers to the Lord.
A strange land () = a Church not his own.
A strange land () = where there is not the Church... The reason a strange land = where there is not the genuine Church, is that... strange = where there is not what is genuine.
Strangers shall swallow it up () = the falsities which will consume it. ( = falsities from evil which will consume it. AC 9995:end.)
A stranger they do not follow, because they know not the voice of strangers ()... The voice of strangers = what is false.
No stranger shall eat of the holy thing () = not those who within the Church do not acknowledge the Lord; thus who are not in the truths and goods of the Church.

A stranger shall not eat () = no appropriation of good with those who do not acknowledge the Lord; for a stranger, and a foreigner, = those who are outside the Church; and those are said to be outside the Church who do not acknowledge the Lord. Explained.
Ye shall not make strange incense to ascend upon it () = no worship from any other love than that of the Lord... Strange = one who is within the Church and does not acknowledge the Lord.

He who shall give of the (ointment) upon a stranger () = conjunction with those who do not acknowledge the Lord, thus who are in evils and the falsities of evil... A stranger = one who is not of the Church, thus who does not acknowledge the Lord, consequently one who is in evils and falsities. For he who does not acknowledge the Lord is not of the Church; and he who denies the Lord is in evils and falsities... That strangers = such. Illustrated.

That strangers = those who do not acknowledge the Lord, and do not want to acknowledge Him, whether outside the Church or within it; thus who are in evils and the falsities of evil; and, in a sense abstracted from persons, evils and the falsities of evil. Illustrated.
Your ground, strangers shall devour it before you () = that evils and the falsities of evil (will consume) the Church.
Foreigners is expressed, in the Original, by a different word from strangers.
The phantasy in which those are who care for nothing else than things not their own, but strange, and who run about seeking them.
Strangers = falsities. AE 518:20. AE 654:40.
Strangers = falsities from evil. AE 654:35.
Strangers () = the natural. Explained.
A stranger = one who is not of the Church.
A man a stranger () = falsity of doctrine.
Under Foreigner, see this reference.
